Pydantic.desc: Python validation library for typed models, parsing, serialization, and schema-driven application contracts. AI/ML Web Feeds uses Pydantic schemas to validate feed metadata and keep submitted YAML data well typed.

PydanticAI.name: PydanticAI
PydanticAI.desc: Pydantic's Python agent framework for typed tools, structured output, providers, and evaluations. Frame Payments uses PydanticAI for typed AI workflows around document intelligence, validation, and agent-oriented application code.

Pytest.name: Pytest
Pytest.desc: Python testing framework for concise unit, integration, fixture, and parametrized test suites. Pytest is Python flexible test runner for unit, fixture, parameterized, and service-level checks.

Python.name: Python
Python.desc: General-purpose language used across Wyatt's AI, data engineering, MCP, SDK, and analytics projects. Python is the common implementation thread behind the basketball database, AI utilities, MCP work, SDK tooling, and analytics.

Python SDKs.name: Python SDKs
Python SDKs.desc: Python client libraries that package APIs, data access, and developer workflows into reusable interfaces. JPMorgan delivered a Python SDK so traders could access a centralized asset-fee data sink without manual data maintenance.

PyTorch.name: PyTorch
PyTorch.desc: Deep-learning framework for tensor computation, autograd, neural networks, and model deployment workflows. PyTorch is a Python deep-learning framework for tensor computation, neural networks, training loops, and research-to-product modeling.

q.name: q
q.desc: Vector-oriented language used with KDB+ for concise, high-speed time-series analytics. JPMorgan market-data work used q with KDB+ for high-performance capital-markets queries and analytics functions.

qPython.name: qPython
qPython.desc: Python interface for communicating with KDB+/q processes from Python systems. JPMorgan work bridged Python workflows with KDB+/q systems through Python wrappers and market-data access tooling.

R.name: R
R.desc: Statistical computing language for analysis, visualization, modeling, and data-science workflows. R is a statistical programming language for modeling, data analysis, visualization, and research-style workflows.

React.name: React
React.desc: Component-based JavaScript library for building interactive interfaces across web, desktop, and plugin surfaces. React appears across Stealth Web3 Startup, Listentropy, Personal Website, MDXPad, and IINA Bookmarks Plugin work.

Real-Time Data Processing.name: Real-Time Data Processing
Real-Time Data Processing.desc: Processing records as they arrive so operational decisions, dashboards, or downstream systems stay current. Real-time processing handles events as they arrive, keeping alerts, dashboards, and downstream services current instead of batch-delayed.

Redis Pub/Sub.name: Redis Pub/Sub
Redis Pub/Sub.desc: Redis messaging primitive for lightweight topic-based publish/subscribe communication. Redis Pub/Sub is lightweight in-memory message broadcasting, useful for simple fan-out patterns where persistence is not the main need.

Redshift.name: Redshift
Redshift.desc: AWS cloud data warehouse for SQL analytics, reporting, and large-scale analytical queries. Redshift is AWS managed data warehouse for analytical SQL workloads, reporting, and large structured datasets.

Redux.name: Redux
Redux.desc: Predictable state-management library for JavaScript applications with explicit actions and centralized stores. Redux centralizes client-side state updates, useful for complex React apps where many views depend on shared application state.

Regularized Regression.name: Regularized Regression
Regularized Regression.desc: Linear modeling with penalty terms such as Ridge, Lasso, and Elastic Net to improve stability and generalization. Wyatt published and open-sourced a regularized linear regression deep dive covering Ridge, Lasso, and Elastic Net.

RESTful APIs.name: RESTful APIs
RESTful APIs.desc: HTTP API style using resources, methods, status codes, and representations for service integration. JPMorgan built an on-demand REST API that exposed centralized asset-fee data to traders and analytics workflows.

Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).name: Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG)
Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG).desc: Pattern where an LLM retrieves trusted external context before generating an answer. Frame Payments document intelligence and NotebookLM work use retrieval to ground answers in uploaded files, vendor docs, and internal sources.

Rust.name: Rust
Rust.desc: Systems programming language emphasizing memory safety, performance, and explicit ownership. Rust is a systems language focused on memory safety and performance, useful for CLIs, services, and native tooling.

scikit-learn.name: scikit-learn
scikit-learn.desc: Python machine-learning library for classical modeling, preprocessing, metrics, and model-selection workflows. The regularized regression project compares custom Ridge, Lasso, and Elastic Net implementations against scikit-learn behavior.

Security-Aware Development.name: Security-Aware Development
Security-Aware Development.desc: Building with attention to secrets, identity, privacy, validation, and misuse-resistant workflows. Frame Payments work combines PII safeguards, confidential-document handling, auditability, and regulated fintech workflows.

Semantic Retrieval.name: Semantic Retrieval
Semantic Retrieval.desc: Meaning-based search that uses embeddings or semantic matching instead of only exact keywords. Frame Payments uses retrieval patterns that search meaning rather than exact keywords across documents and technical knowledge sources.

Serverless Architecture.name: Serverless Architecture
Serverless Architecture.desc: Cloud design model using managed functions and services to reduce server management and scale on demand. JPMorgan describes a cloud-function-driven asset-fee data sink, without naming a vendor-specific serverless runtime.

shadcn/ui.name: shadcn/ui
shadcn/ui.desc: Copyable React component patterns built on Radix UI and Tailwind CSS. Portfolio and developer-facing UI work uses shadcn/ui patterns for polished accessible components without heavy design-system overhead.

SPARQL.name: SPARQL
SPARQL.desc: Query language for RDF knowledge graphs and linked entity relationships. SPARQL queries RDF graphs, making it the SQL-like language for semantic web and knowledge-graph data.

SQL.name: SQL
SQL.desc: Query language for relational databases, analytical stores, schema work, and data access layers. SQL is the standard language for querying, modeling, and transforming relational data across warehouses and application databases.

SQLAlchemy.name: SQLAlchemy
SQLAlchemy.desc: Python SQL toolkit and ORM for database access, query construction, and schema-aware application code. NBA Basketball Database uses SQLAlchemy around validated dataset generation and SQL-backed warehouse workflows.

SQLite.name: SQLite
SQLite.desc: Embedded relational database used for local state, portable datasets, and lightweight application storage. NBA Basketball Database publishes SQLite exports, while ProxyWhirl uses SQLite-backed state for proxy rotation workflows.

Statistical Modeling.name: Statistical Modeling
Statistical Modeling.desc: Using statistical assumptions, model structure, and diagnostics to explain or predict observed data. Statistical modeling estimates relationships in data, giving forecasting and regression work a way to quantify uncertainty and effects.

Structured Logging.name: Structured Logging
Structured Logging.desc: Logging with consistent fields and machine-readable context so events can be searched, correlated, and audited. Structured logging records events as fields rather than prose, making runtime behavior easier to search, filter, and correlate.

Swift.name: Swift
Swift.desc: Apple ecosystem programming language for iOS, macOS, and native application development. Swift is Apple language for iOS and macOS apps, combining native UI development with modern type safety.

Tableau.name: Tableau
Tableau.desc: Business-intelligence platform for interactive dashboards, visual analytics, and stakeholder-facing reporting. Tableau is a BI tool for interactive dashboards and stakeholder reporting, downstream from clean warehouse or extract data.

Tailwind CSS.name: Tailwind CSS
Tailwind CSS.desc: Utility-first CSS framework for composing responsive, token-driven interface styles. Wyatt used Tailwind CSS in public web and portfolio projects, including SandLabs and personal-site work.

TensorFlow.name: TensorFlow
TensorFlow.desc: Machine-learning platform for training, evaluating, and deploying neural-network models. TensorFlow is a neural-network framework for training and serving models, another route into deep learning beside PyTorch.

Terraform.name: Terraform
Terraform.desc: Infrastructure-as-code tool for declaratively provisioning cloud and platform resources. Terraform defines infrastructure in code, so cloud resources can be planned, reviewed, and changed repeatably.

Test-Driven Development.name: Test-Driven Development
Test-Driven Development.desc: Development approach that uses tests to define expected behavior before or alongside implementation. Test-driven development writes expected behavior before implementation, making requirements executable as the code evolves.

Time-Series Forecasting.name: Time-Series Forecasting
Time-Series Forecasting.desc: Forecasting ordered observations over time using decomposition, trend, seasonality, and error-correction techniques. Gap forecasting work used decomposition and bias correction to improve demand forecasts for inventory planning.

Tracing.name: Tracing
Tracing.desc: Following requests and operations across service boundaries to debug latency, failures, and workflow behavior. Tracing follows a request across service boundaries, helping teams diagnose latency, retries, and failures in distributed systems.

TypeScript.name: TypeScript
TypeScript.desc: Typed JavaScript used for safer frontend, backend, tooling, and configuration code. TypeScript runs through the React, Vite, agent tooling, docs, and resume-generation codebases to keep UI and data contracts typed.

Unit Testing.name: Unit Testing
Unit Testing.desc: Focused tests that validate small functions, classes, modules, or contracts in isolation. FL Studio MCP Server uses unit tests within a 650+ test suite covering contracts, runtime paths, and tool behavior.

Vercel.name: Vercel
Vercel.desc: Frontend cloud platform for deploying web apps, docs portals, and serverless-backed product experiences. Listentropy and AI/ML Web Feeds use Vercel for hosted frontend delivery, previews, and public project surfaces.

Vercel AI SDK.name: Vercel AI SDK
Vercel AI SDK.desc: TypeScript toolkit for AI apps with model providers, streaming, tools, and structured output. MDXPad uses Vercel AI SDK for multi-provider AI assistance with token tracking and bring-your-own-key support.

Vite.name: Vite
Vite.desc: Fast frontend build tool and dev server for modern JavaScript and TypeScript applications. Vite is a fast frontend build tool and dev server, fitting React and documentation apps that need quick local feedback and modern bundling.

Vitest.name: Vitest
Vitest.desc: Vite-native JavaScript and TypeScript test runner for fast unit and component testing. Vitest is a fast Vite-native test runner for TypeScript and React code, similar in shape to Jest but optimized for Vite projects.

Web Workers.name: Web Workers
Web Workers.desc: Browser background execution primitive for moving heavy processing off the main UI thread. Listentropy uses a Web Worker pipeline to process large Spotify history files in-browser while keeping the UI responsive.

WebSockets.name: WebSockets
WebSockets.desc: Browser and server protocol for bidirectional, persistent real-time communication. WebSockets keep a browser-server channel open, enabling live UI updates for streams, dashboards, collaboration, and agent sessions.

XGBoost.name: XGBoost
XGBoost.desc: Gradient-boosted tree library for high-performing tabular classification, regression, and ranking models. XGBoost is a boosted-tree library for tabular prediction problems, often strong for structured datasets before deep learning is needed.

YAML.name: YAML
YAML.desc: Human-readable data serialization format used for configuration, schemas, docs metadata, and pipeline definitions. AI/ML Web Feeds uses YAML feed schemas, and MDXPad validates YAML frontmatter for authoring workflows.
